apply.title: Application process
apply.html:
1. Choose your programme, level, province and intake. Compare entry requirements, total tuition, campus and co-op structure.
  2. Check that the institution is on IRCC’s Designated Learning Institution (DLI) list. Confirm the exact programme’s PGWP eligibility separately if that matters to your plan.
  3. Ask the university to assess your Bangladesh qualification. For UG, confirm HSC subjects and grades; for PG, confirm bachelor’s degree length, discipline and GPA conversion.
  4. Confirm the programme’s English test, minimum overall and component scores, validity period and any possible MOI waiver directly with admissions.
  5. Apply through the university’s official portal with transcripts, certificates, passport, references, statement, CV/portfolio and translations if required.
  6. Review the written offer, tuition deposit, refund/deferment policy and conditions. Obtain a valid Letter of Acceptance (LOA).
  7. Check whether you need a PAL/TAL or Quebec CAQ. Do not assume an exemption; check the current IRCC rules for your exact programme and institution.
  8. Prepare proof of funds, study plan and supporting documents. Submit the study-permit application online and complete biometrics/medical steps if requested.

Timing: Deadlines differ by institution, programme and intake. IRCC recommends applying well before the programme starts; there is no single national university deadline.

eng.title: English proficiency and Bangladesh study gap
eng.html:
English proficiency

Canada has no single IELTS/TOEFL score that applies to every university. Each institution and programme sets accepted tests, minimum overall score, component scores and test validity. Confirm the exact requirement on the programme page before booking a test.

An MOI (Medium of Instruction) letter is not a nationwide automatic IELTS waiver. Some institutions or programmes may consider it under their own policy; obtain written confirmation from admissions.

Bangladesh qualifications and study gap

HSC subject prerequisites, grade conversion, foundation/pathway requirements and bachelor’s degree equivalency are assessed by the receiving institution. There is no single universal study-gap limit for all Canadian universities. Explain any gap honestly with dated employment, training, caregiving or other supporting evidence where relevant; the institution and visa officer assess the complete case.

Action: email international admissions with your board, qualification, passing year, subjects, grades and intended programme, and request a written assessment.

money.title: Tuition, living costs and budget
money.html:
Published national tuition averages (2025/2026)

Statistics Canada reported average international tuition of CAD 41,746/year for undergraduate and CAD 24,028/year for graduate students. These are national averages, not a university quote; actual fees vary by province, institution and programme.

Statistics Canada: Tuition in Canada, 2025/2026

IRCC living-funds minimum

For study-permit applications made on or after 1 September 2026, a single applicant studying outside Quebec must show CAD 23,448 for one year of living expenses, in addition to first-year tuition and transportation. The amount changes with family size; Quebec has separate rules. This is an immigration minimum, not a complete budget for every city.

visa.title: Canada study permit
visa.html:
1. Obtain a valid Letter of Acceptance from a DLI.
  2. Check the current PAL/TAL requirement. From 1 January 2026, certain master’s and doctoral students at public DLIs are exempt; other categories and exceptions have separate rules. Quebec applicants may need a CAQ.
  3. Prepare evidence for tuition, living expenses, travel costs and the source/accessibility of funds.
  4. Prepare passport, LOA, required attestation/CAQ, study plan/letter of explanation and any country-specific checklist documents.
  5. Apply online, pay applicable fees and complete biometrics and medical examination if requested.
  6. Wait for the decision and follow the letter/port-of-entry instructions. A study permit is not itself a visa or eTA for travel.

Approval is not guaranteed. Processing time varies; check IRCC’s live tool rather than relying on a fixed estimate.

after.title: Work during study and after graduation
after.html:
Work while studying

Eligible international students may work off campus up to 24 hours per week during regular academic sessions. During regularly scheduled breaks, eligible students may work unlimited hours. You must meet all study-permit conditions; some students/programmes are not eligible. Exceeding the permitted limit can affect your status.

IRCC: Work off campus as an international student

Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)

Graduation from a DLI does not automatically make a student PGWP-eligible. The exact institution and programme must qualify. General requirements include an eligible programme of at least 8 months (Quebec programme rules can differ), maintaining required full-time status, and applying within 180 days of confirmation of completion.

Many applicants must also meet language requirements; eligible non-degree programmes may have field-of-study rules. Requirements depend on credential type and the date of the study-permit application. Check the current IRCC eligibility page before choosing a programme or relying on a post-study work route.

IRCC: PGWP eligibility

schol.title: Scholarships and funding
schol.html:
Search the official Government of Canada EduCanada scholarship database and each university’s international-student awards page. Funding may be merit-based, need-based, programme-specific or research-supervisor-funded. Eligibility, country restrictions, award value and deadlines differ; many awards require a separate application.

  • Check entrance scholarships automatically considered with admission and awards requiring a separate form.
  • For research master’s/PhD programmes, contact prospective supervisors and departments about assistantships, grants and funded positions.
  • Confirm whether an award covers tuition only or also living costs, travel and insurance.
  • Never pay an agent or third party to “guarantee” a scholarship or visa.
